In that case, we found the problem! It's a driver issue. This is likely caused because mint is based on ubuntu LTS release (currently 14.04), while the current non LTS release is 15.10 (IIRC).

Also, before you reboot, make sure the file /etc/X11/xorg.conf exists and is not empty, otherwise your system may not boot to GUI. If it is empty, you can use nvidia-xconfig (in a terminal) to generate it, although you will probably need to adjust the settings after rebooting using the nvidia settings GUI.

NOTE: If you uninstall the driver after installation for any reason, you will be running on the open source drivers, and will need to re-install the LM packaged version of the nvidia driver via the normal "additional drivers" method.

The file is /etc/X11/xorg.conf, I'm not sure if that was a typo or not.

You need to run nvidia-xconfig as root, for example sudo nvidia-xconfig. You will then be prompted for your password. If you have not used sudo before, you should know that it will not give you feedback as you type your password (the letters wont show up, and you won't get asterisks or anything), to prevent people from reading it over your shoulder.

The reason you are getting this error is because /etc is a system folder, which holds important stuff for the OS (think System32 on Windows). Normally, you can't modify it for safety reasons. By running the command as the root user (sometimes called the super user, or admin), the system assumes you know what you are doing. Fun fact: "sudo" stands for "super user do"
